title: Roadmap: context-footprint budget — measure first, then cut tool results, per-prompt overhead, the tool list and the grounding block
context: Measured 2026-09-20 on published 1.39.3 in the hunch repo (chars/4 estimate): tools/list 85,584 chars = ~21.4k tok (12.7k without outputSchema; 6 tools carry 7.6k of outputSchema; hunch_context ~4.0k, hunch_change_proof ~3.0k); generated grounding block 9,714 chars = ~2.4k tok, 61% of CLAUDE.md, written to five files; ~1.8k tok per prompt (hook text ~300 + task start ~250 + task finish ~1.2k, the last two estimated); hunch_context(src/mcp/server.ts) returns ~9.2k tok for a 1,500-token budget because structuredContent carries a 21k-char `omitted` list (104 entries of one repeated sentence) and repeats the brief; hunch_findings() unscoped = ~6.3k tok with no budget; pre-edit hook up to ~1.5k tok per file. Nothing measures any of this, so it grows unseen. David asked on 2026-09-20 to put the optimizations next on the roadmap. Issues: #368 tool list, #369 grounding block, #370 per-prompt overhead, #371 tool results, #372 measurement gate.
decision: Treat context as a budgeted resource with a gate, in this order: (1) #372 ship the measurement (`hunch doctor --context` or equivalent) plus size assertions in tests, so every later cut is proven and cannot regress; (2) #371 make budget_tokens govern the WHOLE tool result — omitted records become counts by reason, the brief is not duplicated between content and structuredContent, list tools (hunch_findings, hunch_now) return a compact list view with a limit; (3) #370 per-prompt overhead — conditional agent-side task calls (dec_0bf3bda2c1), generic guidance once per session, compact finish result; (4) #368 tool list — shrink/drop outputSchema, trim descriptions, consider a small default tool profile with the rest opt-in; (5) #369 slim the grounding block and move the reporting protocol into the hunch_task start response. Proposed targets, to be confirmed by the human: tools/list <= 8k tok, grounding block <= 1k tok, per-prompt <= 400 tok when the task does not use Hunch, any tool result <= 1.5x its budget. Every change must hold for all MCP hosts, not one client.
consequences: Tool descriptions and the grounding block are trigger surfaces: trimming them can lower correct tool selection — the tool-selection audit (dec_39bc7c8bee) must be re-run after #368/#369.
A branch that changes renderHunchSection gets its grounding files reverted by the post-commit capture rendering from the pinned published template (finding fnd_f6875f475b) — handle before #369.
structuredContent shape of hunch_context changes (omitted list -> counts): versioned envelope, check the VS Code extension and any consumer of hunch.delivery-envelope/1.
alternatives_rejected: Rely on host-side tool deferral (Claude Code loads only names): rejected — Codex, Cursor and Windsurf load every schema, and deferral does nothing for hook text, the grounding block or tool results.

Cut the tool list first because it is the biggest single number: rejected as the FIRST step — it is a one-time cost per session, while tool results and per-prompt overhead recur (one hunch_context call costs more than the whole grounding block); and without the measurement gate no cut is provable or protected.
Lower the default budget_tokens: rejected — the text already respects the budget; the overrun is the envelope around it.
Remove delivery receipts / omitted-record accounting: rejected — the accounting stays in the receipt and `hunch report`; only its copy into the model's context goes.
